## Replacement

Replacing the framework (for example with another .NET test framework) replaces this module: new rule facet, commands, enforcement data, knowledge content, and the selection-record row. Workflows refer only to `backend-testing.*` facets and need no edits. Changing the selection is Reserved and requires an ADR.

canonical_policy.name: Choose narrowest useful test level
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Choose the narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behavior; use integration tests when framework/persistence/HTTP wiring is the subject; no fixed unit/integration ratio is required.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Narrowest meaningful level coexists with full-suite small-solution procedure and limited meaningful frontend E2E defaults. These added scope rules are explicit prior actions.

context_quotes:
paths:
  - "backend/**/*Tests/**/*"
---

- Default: choose the narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behavior — unit tests for isolated logic, integration tests when framework wiring, HTTP, persistence, serialization, authentication, or component interaction is the subject. No fixed unit/integration ratio is required.
- Test observable behavior, not implementation details: write tests that survive internal refactoring; do not assert private calls or incidental call sequences or reproduce the implementation's algorithm. Interaction checks fit only when the interaction is the specified behavior.

Test meaningful component behavior, validation, data-access request mapping, important route/auth behavior, and complex reactive state with the configured runner; do not test framework internals. E2E covers a few important user workflows unless broader coverage is required; avoid duplicating the same behavior at every level.

Prefer one observable scenario per test; a multi-step test fits when the sequence is the scenario (a whole workflow or replace-set lifecycle).

Good unit candidates: non-trivial domain behavior that genuinely belongs to the domain model, calculations, workflow/state transitions at their owning layer, validation logic, orchestration with simple fakes. Replace persistence-access contracts and external abstractions with controlled doubles; assert the use-case result and meaningful side effects. "Method X was called once" is useful only when that interaction is the contract. When behavior depends on ORM semantics, transactions, DI wiring, serialization, or HTTP, prefer an integration test over reproducing the stack with mocks. Do not mock every collaborator mechanically, and do not forbid mocking project-owned abstractions when isolation helps.

Metadata disagreeing with runtime; public Swagger UI without a reason; Swagger as a substitute for integration tests; global auth requirements on anonymous endpoints; anonymous objects as long-lived contracts; a second competing documentation stack without need.

Run tests covering the changed area (`backend-testing.commands`; frontend: the configured test script per `frontend.commands`). For small solutions run the full suite; for large ones run affected test projects first, then any broader suite the change risk requires. Investigate every newly failing relevant test — do not dismiss a failure as unrelated without checking it.

| Use-case persistence dependency | specific repository interface |
| Commit | `IUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync` |
| Read-only entity query | `AsNoTracking()` when useful |
| Read model | database-side projection |
| Primary-key entity lookup | `FindAsync` when its semantics fit |
| Complex graph | explicit `Include` or projection |
| Set-based update/delete | `ExecuteUpdateAsync` / `ExecuteDeleteAsync` when appropriate |
| Measured extremely hot query | consider a compiled query |
| Several commits that must be atomic | explicit transaction |
| Production schema change | reviewed migration, controlled deployment |
| Empty Development database | run the seeder |
| Fresh local seed data | explicitly recreate the local database |
| Test data | dedicated test setup, never the seeder |

Do not request duplicate tests when equivalent coverage exists.
**Bug fix** — Default: for a meaningful bug with plausible recurrence, add a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it, unless equivalent coverage already exists.

| External HTTP dependency | stub `HttpMessageHandler` or a local fake server |
| Reproduced bug | focused regression test |
| Temporary behavioral probe | convert it to maintained coverage or confirm equivalent coverage exists |

A regression test reproduces the failure before the fix and passes after it. Converting a temporary probe: a curl, PowerShell, or REST check becomes a host integration test; a manual database check becomes a persistence test; reuse existing coverage when it already exercises the behavior, after confirming it really does.
